lhs.note: lhs is the left operand of a reflected less-than (Parameter.__rlt__(self, lhs)); it is whatever live object Python places on the left of `<` when the right side is a Parameter. Seeded with one real Parameter instance and three non-Parameter primitives (int/float/str).

Parameter.note: The class object used as the isinstance() second arg; a constant, not an input.

encoding: isinstance(lhs, Parameter) is a unary runtime type-test, not an arithmetic/comparison/boolean op over a scalar input -- it is outside the ExpressionEvaluator scalar op-surface. z3 cannot derive an object's runtime type from first principles, so the predicate is modeled as a finite enum: lhs ranges over the 4 seeded values (z3 Datatype Lhs = {v_param, v_42, v_314, v_hello}), with a tag function is_parameter(Lhs)->Bool pinned to ground truth obtained from an in-container isinstance probe (v_param=True, others=False). pred = is_parameter(lhs). This is a bounded model over the seeded enum -- the type tags are supplied by the runtime, not proven by the solver -- hence solver_status=unknown / classification=runtime-dependent per the isinstance-on-live-object rule.

z3_output.note: Bounded over the seeded enum with ground-truth type tags pinned. Both branch sides are reachable (sat). The solver decides which enum element is selected; it does NOT decide the isinstance result itself -- that tag is harvested from the live Python probe below.

python_ground_truth.probe: from Tensile.Configuration import Parameter; isinstance(val, Parameter) run in-container (cwd=tensilelite, PYTHONPATH set)

notes: Branch at Configuration.py:224 is the guard inside Parameter.__rlt__(self, lhs): `if isinstance(lhs, Parameter): return lhs.value < self.value` else `return lhs < self.value`. The predicate's truth is fixed entirely by the RUNTIME TYPE of the live left operand, not by any public CLI/yaml/int/bool value, so it is runtime-dependent (solver_status=unknown). z3 was actually run in-container and returns BOTH sides sat over the seeded enum (TRUE: lhs=v_param; FALSE: lhs=v_42), but only because the per-element type tags were pinned from a live isinstance probe -- the solver cannot prove an object's class on its own. Representative witnesses by value: TRUE = a Parameter instance Parameter(name=x, initialValue=1) (then the guard compares .value attributes: lhs.value < self.value); FALSE = any non-Parameter (42 / 3.14 / 'hello') (then bare lhs < self.value, which for str-vs-int would itself raise TypeError -- a separate downstream behavior, not this guard). No PURE helper extractable for CrossHair: the predicate is a single bare isinstance type-test with no relational postcondition to falsify; the would-be helper `def is_param(x): return isinstance(x, Parameter)` has no nontrivial contract, and CrossHair cannot synthesize arbitrary live class instances anyway -- absence of a counterexample would not be a proof. The load-bearing evidence is the in-container Python ground-truth probe plus the bounded z3 reachability check.
